plain.headline: God Invites Everyone to the Feast
plain.intro: Today's readings describe God's kingdom as a great banquet. Isaiah sees a feast for all peoples where death is gone for good, and Jesus tells a parable about a king's wedding feast that many guests refuse. Between them, Psalm 23 and Saint Paul speak of a God who provides what we need, and who asks us to answer his invitation with our whole lives.
plain.listen: the invitation to the feast, and how each guest answers it

Reading 1.box: Isaiah pictures God hosting a rich feast on his mountain for every nation. At that feast God removes the grief that hangs over the world, ends death forever, and dries every tear. This passage comes from a part of Isaiah that looks ahead to the end of time, and Christians hear in it a promise fulfilled in Christ.

chunks.text: On this mountain the Lord of hosts will throw a feast for all peoples, with the best meat and the finest wine. On this mountain he will tear away the shroud that covers every people, the veil spread over all the nations.
He will destroy death forever. The Lord God will wipe the tears from every face. He will remove the shame of his people everywhere on earth. The Lord has said it.
On that day people will say, "Look, this is our God. We waited for him, and he saved us. This is the Lord we waited for. Let us be glad and celebrate that he has saved us."
The Lord's hand will rest on this mountain. But Moab, an enemy nation, will be trampled down where it stands, like straw trampled into a muddy manure pit.

Responsorial Psalm.box: Psalm 23 calls the Lord a shepherd who leads us to rest, stays with us in the darkest valley, and sets a table for us. It ends with the hope of living in God's house forever.

Reading 2.box: Paul writes to the Christians in Philippi to thank them for a gift they sent him while he was in prison. He says he has learned to be at peace whether he has plenty or very little, because Christ gives him strength. He trusts God to care for them just as they cared for him.

chunks.text: I know what it is to have little, and I know what it is to have plenty. In every situation I have learned the secret of being full and being hungry, of having more than enough and having too little.
I can do anything through Christ, who gives me strength. Still, it was good of you to share in my hardship.
My God will give you everything you need, out of his great riches in Christ Jesus. Glory to our God and Father forever and ever. Amen.

Gospel.box: Jesus tells this parable in Jerusalem to the religious leaders who were rejecting him. A king invites guests to his son's wedding, but they refuse and even kill his messengers, so he opens the feast to everyone on the streets. One guest comes without wedding clothes and is thrown out. Many teachers in the Church have understood the wedding clothes as a life changed by God's grace: the invitation is free, and it asks for a real response.

chunks.text: Jesus spoke to them again in parables. He said, "The kingdom of heaven is like a king who gave a wedding feast for his son.

He sent his servants to call the invited guests to the feast, but they refused to come. So he sent more servants and told them, 'Tell the guests: My dinner is prepared. My cattle and fattened animals are butchered, and everything is ready. Come to the wedding feast.'
But the guests shrugged it off and went about their business, one to his farm and another to his shop. The rest seized the king's servants, abused them, and killed them.
When the king heard this, he was furious. He sent his troops, destroyed those murderers, and burned their city.
Then he told his servants, 'The wedding feast is ready, but the guests I invited did not deserve it. So go out to the main roads and invite everyone you find.'
The servants went out to the roads and brought in everyone they found, bad and good alike, and the wedding hall filled with guests.
When the king came in to see the guests, he noticed a man who was not dressed for a wedding. He said to him, 'Friend, how did you get in here without wedding clothes?' The man had nothing to say.
Then the king told the attendants, 'Tie him hand and foot and throw him out into the darkness, where there will be weeping and grinding of teeth.' Many are invited, but few are chosen."

plain.carry: God has already invited me to his table, and this week I can answer by how I live, not only by showing up.

kids.headline: You Are Invited
kids.intro: Today we hear about a giant party that God is getting ready for all people. Jesus tells a story about a king who invites guests to his son's wedding, and we learn what it means to say yes to God.
kids.listen: Listen for the king's wedding party, and who says yes and who says no.

Reading 1.box: The prophet Isaiah tells us about a wonderful feast God will give on a mountain for people from every land. At this feast God will take away sadness, wipe away tears, and make death go away forever.

chunks.text: On his mountain, God will make a feast for everyone, with the best food and drink. He will take away the sadness that covers the whole world like a heavy blanket. He will end death forever and wipe the tears from every face.

People will say, "This is our God. We waited for him, and he saved us. Let's be happy." God's hand will rest on his mountain. Moab, a nation that fought against God's people, will be beaten down like straw stamped into mud.

Responsorial Psalm.box: This psalm says God is like a good shepherd who takes care of us, stays with us when we are scared, and gives us all we need.

Reading 2.box: Saint Paul was in prison when he wrote this letter. His friends in a town called Philippi sent him help, and he thanks them. He says Jesus makes him strong whether he has a lot or a little.

chunks.text: Sometimes I have had very little, and sometimes I have had plenty. I have been full, and I have been hungry. I can do anything with the help of Jesus, who makes me strong. Thank you for helping me when times were hard.
God will give you everything you need, because he is so rich in love through Jesus. Glory to God our Father forever. Amen.

Gospel.box: Jesus tells a story about a king who throws a wedding party for his son. The first guests say no, so the king invites everyone he can find. Jesus wants us to know that God invites all of us, and that saying yes means letting God change our hearts.

chunks.text: Jesus told a story. He said, "Heaven is like a king who gave a wedding party for his son. He sent his servants to bring the guests he had invited, but they would not come.

The king sent more servants to say, 'The food is cooked and everything is ready. Come to the party.' But the guests did not care. One went to his farm and one went to his store. Others grabbed the servants, hurt them badly, and killed them.

The king was very angry. He sent his soldiers to punish those killers and burn their city. Then he told his servants, 'The party is ready, but those guests did not deserve to come. Go out to the roads and invite everyone you see.' So the servants brought in everyone they found, bad people and good people, and the hall was full.

When the king came in, he saw a man who was not wearing wedding clothes. The king asked, 'Friend, how did you get in without wedding clothes?' The man had no answer. So the king had him tied up and sent out into the dark, where people cry and are very sorry. Many people are invited, but only a few are chosen."

word.meaning: A feast is a big, joyful meal with lots of good food, shared to celebrate something special.

kids.draw: Draw the king's wedding party with a long table full of food and people from everywhere sitting together.
kids.ask: If God sent you an invitation, how would you say yes?

family.opener: Today Jesus tells a story about a wedding party where some guests say no to the invitation, so let's think about how we answer when God invites us.
questions: What is the best party or meal you have ever been invited to, and what made it special?
Why do you think the first guests said no to the king?
What might it look like for our family to come to God's feast ready, like wearing wedding clothes?
family.try: Invite someone to share a meal with your family this week, especially someone who might not get many invitations.
family.pray: Good Shepherd, thank you for inviting us to your table; help us say yes to you with our whole lives.
